organizations.csv: Key quality for the load: `acct_num` is blank on 13 rows and has 18 duplicate values (999 distinct over 1030 rows). Because organization.organization_id is required and unique, and re-sending an id with different content is a 409 conflict, the engineer must decide at validation whether duplicates are merged, suffixed, or held back; blank-key rows cannot be loaded as organizations at all (and any contact/activity derived from them would be orphaned).

`company_name` shows 45 normalized duplicates and 11 case-variant groups, so some of the 18 duplicate account numbers are probably genuine duplicate accounts rather than reused ids. Worth a de-duplication pass before load.

Future-dated values: 4 rows in `created_on` and 5 rows in `last_activity_date` fall after today (range ends 2027-09-03). Future dates in `last_activity_date` will also suppress the rule 2 dormancy override for those accounts.

Cross-record rule check: 'an inactive or churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription'. Mapping 'On Hold' to active (rule 6) avoids that conflict, but the rule 2 dormancy override will demote some CRM-Active accounts to inactive; if those accounts still have active subscriptions in the billing export, the subscription load will be rejected. The engineer should reconcile the derived lifecycle_status against the subscription file before loading.

Contact creation from `primary_contact_email` (customer rule 1) is incomplete on its own: contact.first_name and contact.last_name are required in the target and this dataset has no contact name column (`account_owner` is an internal rep, not the contact). Names must come from the contacts file, or a deterministic placeholder/derivation from the email local part has to be agreed.

`primary_contact_email` has 30 normalized duplicates across accounts. Meridian only requires email uniqueness within an organization, so cross-account duplicates are acceptable; duplicates within the same acct_num would need resolution at validation.

Assumption recorded: organization.billing_region is used for `hq_state` and organization.customer_since for `created_on` because the target has no separate HQ-address or record-creation-date fields. If Apex distinguishes HQ from billing address, or account creation from relationship start, those distinctions are lost in this migration.

Customer rules 7-12 (plan and billing-cycle vocabularies, quarterly conversion, dead trials, CAD amounts) and rule 13 (contact role vocabulary) refer to fields not present in this dataset; they apply to the subscription and contact files.
contacts.csv: contact.organization_id is required, but `acct_num` is null on 22 rows (1.0%); those contacts have no organization to attach to and the cross-record rules require the organization to exist first. Handling (reject, park, or manual assignment) is a validation-time decision for the engineer.

contact.email is required and 106 values (4.7%) are malformed, plus 66 normalized duplicates across the file; after lower-casing, duplicates that fall within the same acct_num will violate the 'email unique within an organization' rule. Worth a de-duplication pass before load.

Roughly 942 rows carry a truthy `is_primary` value across only 1046 distinct accounts, so some organizations will have more than one primary and others none. Meridian allows at most one is_primary=true per organization (hard rule) and warns when an organization with contacts has none. A deterministic tie-break is needed at load time; customer rule 1 says the account row's `primary_contact_email` is authoritative where the CRM has no primary flag, but that column is on the accounts dataset and not in contacts.csv, so this reconciliation must be done across the two files.

`last_touch` has 8 dates in the future (range extends to 2027-08-05) and only 16.6% of values are ISO; if the customer chooses to migrate these dates, parsing must be format-aware (%Y/%m/%d, %B %d, %Y, %Y-%m-%d, %d-%b-%Y, %m/%d/%y, %m/%d/%Y) and %m/%d/%y two-digit years need a pivot rule.

`full_name` maps to two required target fields; the loader must write both contact.first_name and contact.last_name from this single column. 88 normalized duplicate names exist, which is normal for person names and not by itself a duplicate-record signal.

Assumption: the opt-out preference (214 'Y') is not carried into Meridian because no target field exists; it should stay in the customer's marketing system. Flag this to the customer if they expect suppression lists to be enforced from Meridian.
subscriptions.json: acct_num has 903 distinct values over 1003 rows, so roughly 100 accounts hold more than one subscription. Every acct_num must resolve to an organization created from the accounts dataset before load (cross-record rule: an organization must exist before a subscription references it).

Rule 11 (trial subscriptions older than 90 days are not migrated) is a row filter, not a field mapping: 84 rows have sub_status 'trialing' and 27 have subscription_level 'Trial'. The rule does not state the reference date or which date it measures - we assume start_dt measured against the migration cutover date; confirm with the engineer before excluding rows, and note the two sets of rows may not be identical.

Rule 7 (Legacy Gold -> enterprise unless seats < 10) cannot be evaluated for Legacy Gold rows whose seat_count is null (41 nulls overall, 4.1%). The default for those rows is a validation-time decision; enterprise is the safer default since it is the stated base rule.

Rule 4 says Strategic accounts always carry an Enterprise subscription and that billing is wrong where it disagrees. If the accounts dataset flags Strategic accounts whose subscription_level here maps to starter or professional, the plan value will have to be overridden at load; this cross-dataset override is not visible in this file alone.

Cross-record rule: an inactive or churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription. Rule 2 (dormant accounts become Inactive) and rule 6 (Closed = churned) will likely produce such conflicts for the 611 active and 84 trialing rows here; the reconciliation between account lifecycle and subscription status needs to be resolved during load.

start_dt has 2 future values and renew_dt has 81 (range to 2027) - future renewal dates are expected, future start dates are not; flag them at validation rather than at mapping. The catalog also requires renewal_date > start_date, which cannot be verified from these statistics.
monthly_amount has a minimum of 0, so some subscriptions will load with mrr_usd = 0; confirm at validation whether zero-revenue subscriptions (trials, internal accounts) should still be migrated.
activity.csv: Referential integrity: acct_num holds 1000 distinct accounts across 4947 activities. Load organizations first (cross-record rule: an organization must exist before any activity references it) and reconcile the 1000 values against the account dataset's organization_id set before loading activities; any unmatched account number will reject at load.

occurred_at ranges to 2026-09-11, i.e. timestamps in the future relative to a typical migration date. Confirm with the engineer whether these are scheduled/forecast records (e.g. future-dated invoices) or data-entry errors; they also distort the 18-month dormancy window in customer rule 2.

Customer rule 2 (accounts with no activity in the last 18 months are dormant and must be set to Inactive) is computed from this dataset: derive max(occurred_at) per acct_num and feed it into organization.lifecycle_status. Decide whether future-dated rows count as 'recent activity', and whether accounts with zero rows in activity.csv (none of the 1000 are missing here, but accounts absent from this file entirely) are dormant by definition.

Amount coverage is consistent with the activity kinds: 2563 rows have a currency and 2563 rows are Invoice+INVOICE+Payment, of which 650 amount values are placeholders that become null. So roughly 650 invoice/payment activities will land with amount_usd = null; activity.amount_usd is nullable, so this loads, but flag it to finance if invoice totals are reconciled after go-live.
activity_type has one case-variant group (Invoice vs INVOICE, 1489 rows combined); case folding is handled in the field transformation and does not change record counts.
No blank or duplicate activity_id values and no exact duplicate rows, so id-based idempotency (re-sending an id with identical content is a no-op) is safe for this dataset.

rows.reason: Declared key column of the dataset and the catalog states the customer's legacy account number usually lands in organization.organization_id; the 5-digit numeric values satisfy the target pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$.
Exact semantic and name match to the required organization.name; free-text company names up to 34 chars fit the target.

This is the account-level CRM state, so organization.lifecycle_status is the right home; subscription.status is a different concept (and this dataset carries no subscription). Six of nine values need an enum mapping table and the customer's rule 6 covers the two non-enum business states.
Short industry codes correspond one-to-one with the organization.industry enum; only the two numeric codes are not self-evident, so a mapping table is required.

organization.billing_region is the only state/province field in the target catalog and its description (state or province code, e.g. CA, TX, ON) matches these values; we assume HQ state is acceptable as the billing region since no separate HQ address exists in the target. The value is also needed as input to the country disambiguation in customer rule 5.
Direct semantic match to the required organization.billing_country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2); six of nine value spellings fail the ^[A-Z]{2}$ pattern and customer rule 5 makes 'CA' genuinely ambiguous.
Exact name and type match to organization.website, which is nullable, so the placeholders and blanks are acceptable.

organization.customer_since ('when the relationship started, per the customer's records') is the only organization-level date in the catalog and a CRM account creation date is the usual proxy; no other target field fits.

'Strategic' maps cleanly onto the account_priority enum value 'strategic' per customer rule 3, but Gold/Silver/Bronze are spend bands with no equivalent in the enum (standard/priority/strategic) and the catalog warns account_priority is not the plan; whether spend bands become priority/standard or are preserved as organization.tags is a business decision.
Name and meaning match organization.annual_revenue_usd; the values are currency-formatted text that needs cleaning to satisfy the decimal pattern.
Exact name and meaning match to the nullable integer organization.employee_count.

There is no email field on organization in the catalog, and customer rule 1 states the account-row primary_contact_email is authoritative for creating or flagging the primary contact - so this column belongs on the contact entity, not the organization.

These are internal Apex sales-rep names (993 distinct person names on 1030 rows), not customer contacts; the Meridian catalog has no account-owner or user field on organization, and contact.first_name/last_name are for customer contacts. Nothing in the business rules asks for owner data to be migrated, so it can be dropped.

There is no last-activity field on organization; the only home for it would be an activity record (activity.occurred_at, which also requires activity.kind and a generated activity.activity_id). Whether to synthesize one activity row per account or to use this column only as the input to the dormancy rule is a business decision.

Only 4 distinct values across 568 populated rows, with shapes that look like canned phrases plus something resembling a city/state/ZIP string ('aaaaa AA 9999'); the candidate homes are organization.tags or activity.description, and we cannot tell which without knowing what the four values mean.

Dataset key, 100% unique and never null; the values (CT-000102) satisfy the contact.contact_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as they stand. The deterministic MATCHED call agrees and the meaning (one row per contact) matches.

A 5-digit legacy account number repeated across contacts (1046 distinct over 2279 rows), which is the shape of a foreign key to the account; the catalog says the legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so on a contact row it is contact.organization_id.

Single free-text person name that has to feed the two required target fields contact.first_name and contact.last_name; mapped here to first_name with the split rule, last_name is populated from the same column.
Email-typed column on a contact row mapping to the required contact.email; name and values agree with the deterministic call.
Phone column on the contact row; contact.phone is the only phone field in the catalog and it requires E.164, which the data (0 E.164 values, formats like (999) 999-9999) does not yet use.

Clearly the source for contact.role, but 9 of the 12 values are outside the target enum and customer rule 13 only covers 9 of them; 'Ops Manager', 'Purchasing' and 'Main' are uncovered, and CEO/Owner could reasonably be 'executive' rather than 'primary', so the value table is a business decision.
Exact name and meaning match to the boolean contact.is_primary; only the eight spellings of yes/no need normalizing.

There is no last-contact or last-activity date on contact in the catalog. The only date-like homes are activity.occurred_at (which would mean synthesizing activity records with a kind and an id) and organization.customer_since (a different meaning), so a person has to decide whether this column is migrated at all.

Meridian's contact entity has no marketing-consent or opt-out field, and rule 14 only requires that opted-out contacts still be migrated, not that the flag itself be carried over; organization.tags is the only free field and sits on the wrong entity. No mapping decision is therefore outstanding.
Unique, non-null identifier (1003 distinct of 1003 rows) on a subscription dataset; the SUB-99999 shape satisfies the subscription_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as-is.

Numeric account number with 903 distinct values over 1003 rows, i.e. several subscriptions share one account; on a subscription row this is the foreign key to the account, and the catalog says the customer's legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id.

Plan-name vocabulary that the customer's rules 7 and 8 explicitly translate into the target enum starter/professional/enterprise; the only unresolved part is the 'Trial' value, which names a status rather than a plan.
Direct billing-frequency field for the target enum monthly/annual; every source value is covered by an obvious abbreviation expansion or by the customer's rule 9 on quarterly billing.

Subscription lifecycle values matching the target enum trial/active/past_due/cancelled once case and spelling variants are normalized; rule 10 covers the two values the enum does not have. organization.lifecycle_status is a different concept (the account, not the contract).
Seat quantity for the required integer field subscription.seats; the export types it inconsistently (709 int, 253 str) so only a cast is needed. It also drives the Legacy Gold split in rule 7.
Subscription start date matching the required target date field by name and meaning; only 18.7% of values are already ISO 8601 so the six formats must be parsed.
Renewal date matching the required target field by name and meaning; same six mixed formats, 18.2% ISO, so parsing is required.

Rule 12 states the billing export amounts are monthly regardless of billing frequency, which is exactly the definition of subscription.mrr_usd (monthly recurring revenue in USD); all 1003 values parsed numerically, but 699 are strings with currency decoration.
The subscription entity has only mrr_usd and no currency field, and rule 12 instructs that CAD amounts (75 rows) be migrated as-is into USD, which makes the currency column redundant for the load.
Exact name match to the activity entity's primary key; 4947 distinct values, no nulls or duplicates, and the shape ACT-0003710 satisfies the target pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as-is.

This is the only account reference on the activity row (1000 distinct 5-digit values over 4947 rows), and the catalog notes the customer's legacy account number is what lands in organization.organization_id, so it is the foreign key from activity to organization. The deterministic comparison found no name token overlap, which is a naming difference only.

Name match after synonyms and the value vocabulary (Invoice, Payment, Login, Note, Support Ticket) lines up with the activity.kind enum; only the destination of 'Ticket' (618) and 'Call' (215) is uncertain, which is a value question, not a target question.
Exact name match to the required datetime field on the activity entity; values are timestamps spanning 2016-2026. Only the encoding differs, since just 49.7% are ISO 8601.

Only monetary field on the activity row and the target activity.amount_usd is the nullable decimal for it; the 61.3% nulls are expected because the non-financial kinds (login, note, ticket, call) carry no amount, and the 2563 populated rows equal the Invoice+Payment row count.

The activity entity has no currency field, and the single observed value is USD (2563 rows, the rest blank), so it carries no information the USD-denominated activity.amount_usd does not already imply. Rule 12 also instructs that amounts migrate as-is into USD, making a currency column redundant.

Exact name match to the optional, nullable free-text field on the activity entity; values are short labels (max length 24) that fit the target as they are. The 24.5% blanks are acceptable because the target is nullable.
